intent: One continuous historia; no extended Bible mode, no newly built independent story catalogue. Consolidated movements are navigational editorial planning units, not final public chapters.
rules: Main spine contains all A beats, not full chapter text
B is short contextual stitching, not automatic passage import
C remains optional via pre-existing person/event/Scripture routes only if verified
D never duplicates a featured passage
Keep the exact original pericope, chapter ownership and Gospel differences at source; no new blended verse text
Original biblical books' chronology, especially exile witnesses and Apocalypse, cannot be forced into one literal sequence
Final public chapter count is not selected by an arbitrary numeric target

movements.title: Creation and the human vocation
movements.purpose: The world, humanity made for communion with God, and the Sabbath complete the opening frame

movements.title: The Fall and the First Promise
movements.purpose: Disobedience, death and the first announced victory over evil form one continuous Genesis 3 account

movements.title: Noah, the covenant and the peoples
movements.purpose: Human corruption, judgment, preservation and the rainbow covenant; the nations and Babel close this transition

movements.title: Abraham called into covenant
movements.purpose: God elects Abraham and makes a promise for Israel and all nations

movements.title: Isaac, Jacob and Israel
movements.purpose: The promised line passes through Isaac and Jacob and Israel receives his identity

movements.title: Joseph and the descent into Egypt
movements.purpose: Joseph's providential reconciliation places the family of Israel in Egypt

movements.title: Bondage and the calling of Moses
movements.purpose: Oppression prepares Israel's deliverance and the divine name is revealed

movements.title: Plagues and the first Passover
movements.purpose: God judges Pharaoh, gives the saving Passover and prepares the Exodus

movements.title: Exodus through the sea
movements.purpose: Israel leaves Egypt and passes through the sea toward Sinai; wilderness provision is kept brief

movements.title: Sinai: covenant and unfaithfulness
movements.purpose: Law and blood of covenant meet the golden calf and intercession; the divine dwelling supplies its resolution

movements.title: Israel enters the promised land
movements.purpose: Moses dies, Joshua leads Israel into the land, and the cycle of the Judges explains why kingship follows

movements.title: From Ruth to Samuel and Saul
movements.purpose: The Ruth-to-David family bridge and Israel's request for a king supply the transition from Judges to monarchy

movements.title: David and the enduring royal promise
movements.purpose: David is chosen, receives Jerusalem and the Ark, and hears God's promise of an enduring throne

movements.title: The Temple and the divided kingdom
movements.purpose: The moral frailty of kings, Temple worship, Solomon's infidelity and division after him

movements.title: Prophetic warning and Israel's judgment
movements.purpose: Prophetic voices and messianic promises interpret the divisions and Israel's catastrophe

movements.title: The New Covenant promised in exile
movements.purpose: Jeremiah promises a new covenant; Jerusalem falls, and distinct voices witness exile without forced chronology

movements.title: Restoration and the expectation of Christ
movements.purpose: Exiles return, the Temple is rebuilt, and the period before Christ is oriented by fidelity and hope

movements.title: The generations and the Annunciation
movements.purpose: The Abraham-David-Christ lineage frames the Incarnation; Matthew and Luke remain distinct navigation witnesses

movements.title: The birth of the Saviour
movements.purpose: Joseph accepts Mary's Son, Christ is born, and the Magi signal the Gospel's universal horizon

movements.title: The Forerunner and first disciples
movements.purpose: Jesus is baptized, proclaims the Kingdom and gathers disciples; the first sign is context not a miracle catalogue

movements.title: The Kingdom in Christ's teaching and signs
movements.purpose: The Beatitudes, prayer and forgiveness reveal the Kingdom; use one representative healing, not serial miracle anthologies

movements.title: Christ the Bread of Life
movements.purpose: The sign of the loaves leads to Christ's explicit discourse on the Bread of Life

movements.title: Peter's confession and the Transfiguration
movements.purpose: Peter identifies the Christ and the Transfiguration reveals his glory before the Passion

movements.title: The approach to Jerusalem
movements.purpose: The raising of Lazarus anticipates Christ's death and Resurrection without requiring every Bethany or Jericho encounter

movements.title: The King's entry into Jerusalem
movements.purpose: Christ enters Jerusalem and approaches the Passion

movements.title: The Last Supper and Christ's final teaching
movements.purpose: The Eucharist and new covenant at the Supper; Christ's promise of the Father's house and union with him

movements.title: Gethsemane, betrayal and trial
movements.purpose: Christ accepts the cup, is betrayed and condemned; the Johannine account is separately referenced, not silently merged

movements.title: The sacrifice on Calvary
movements.purpose: The Cross accomplishes the saving death of Christ

movements.title: The risen Lord and his witnesses
movements.purpose: The empty tomb and encounters with Mary Magdalene, the Apostles and Thomas establish the Resurrection

movements.title: The Ascension and promised mission
movements.purpose: Christ ascends and commissions the Apostles for the nations

movements.title: Pentecost and the first Church
movements.purpose: The Holy Ghost descends, the Church forms its common life, and Stephen witnesses unto death

movements.title: Saul and the Gospel to the Gentiles
movements.purpose: Saul is converted and Cornelius is received; no repetition of the same Cornelius event

movements.title: Antioch, apostolic missions and the Council
movements.purpose: Antioch sends missionaries, and the Council settles Gentile inclusion

movements.title: The Gospel proclaimed in Rome
movements.purpose: The universal apostolic mission reaches Rome; individual missionary episodes need not be read in sequence

movements.title: Christ and the Lamb in heavenly vision
movements.purpose: Christ addresses his Church and the slain Lamb stands at the center of God's heavenly plan

movements.title: The final conflict and judgment
movements.purpose: Visionary images of conflict lead to Christ's victory and judgment without a contrived literal timeline

movements.title: The New Creation
movements.purpose: God's renewed dwelling with his people, the river of life and consummation of the promise

continuityChecks.issue: Noah→Abraham requires the descendants through Shem and the passage of generations, not merely an abrupt scene cut.
The judges' recurring cycle needs an explicit hinge from tribal Israel to Samuel and the request for a king; Deborah and Samson are not essential prerequisite biographies.
Ruth 4 genealogy should introduce David's line without requiring full Ruth stories or inventing a chronology with Samuel.
Messianic prophecies in Isaiah are literary witnesses, not one event dated immediately before Samaria's fall. The two kingdoms must stay distinct.
Daniel, Tobit, Judith and Esther are independent witnesses of fidelity, not chronological stages in one exile. Return under Persia cannot presuppose their order.
The time between restoration, the Maccabees and the Incarnation must be introduced succinctly; neither invented dates nor forced overlap.
Matthew 1 and Luke 3 genealogies have distinct order and content: do not read them as a stitched narrative or claim Luke gives Mary's biological descent.
One representative miracle demonstrating authority, such as forgiveness and healing in Mark 2:1–12, prevents a Kingdom narrative consisting only of sayings; John 6 feeding remains once in HS-M22.
The source proposal for farewell teaching stops at John 14:14. The Holy Spirit/Paraclete promise in John 14:16–17 or John 16:7–13 is not yet carried and is a crucial bridge to Pentecost.
Some resurrection appearances occur at different times and in distinct Gospel witnesses; avoid compressing them into a single encounter.
Acts 28:23–31 is not itself Paul's arrival in Rome. Acts 28:16 explicitly describes the arrival; his mission must not appear as a teleport after Acts 15.
Revelation's liturgy, conflict, judgment and new creation are symbolic visions, not episodes falsely dated after Paul's imprisonment. Christ/Lamb remain central; visions not literalized.

sourceBridgeCandidates.scenePurpose: Christ promises the Advocate/Spirit of Truth before the Pentecost narrative
sourceBridgeCandidates.whyRequired: The currently proposed H61 source John 14:1–14 omits the promised Paraclete. A reader could reach Pentecost without Christ's explicitly spoken promise of the Holy Ghost.

sourceBridgeCandidates.scenePurpose: Acts explicitly announces Paul's arrival in Rome before his final uninterrupted proclamation
sourceBridgeCandidates.whyRequired: H73-07 starts at Acts 28:23; without the earlier arrival verse, the main story leaps directly from the Council to an unexplained Roman setting.
